gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of three-camera video a card holds before the loop overwrites it (Vantrue OnDash N4: 30.3 Mb/s measured across front, cabin and rear = 13.6 GB per hour, so 18.8 h on its 256 GB maximum and 2.3 h on a 32 GB card), or that adding the maker's hardwire kit for parking mode puts both the Redtiger A3 ($108.73) and the N4 ($129.98) over $100.
standout_why: Compared against Digital Camera World (cited; no 3-channel camera and no hours, bitrate or kit price in the part of the article the fetch returned, which was cut short), ProductBible (no 3-channel model; its only all-in sum is a 1-channel '$96 camera to about $150'), my-best (only a generic 'the 3 cameras can store around 10 hours of data in total', tied to no model or card; it prices the N4 at $259.99) and deal.ai (prices only). None gives a per-model data rate, loop hours per card size, or a camera-plus-kit total for a 3-channel camera under $100. ChatGPT's own answer says parking recording 'may require' a hardwire kit but gives no price. The Walmart category page ChatGPT cited was not opened.
decides: It confirms the Vantrue OnDash N4 as a row that meets the line on camera price alone ($99.99 at Vantrue on 2026-11-26), with two conditions the page must state: Vantrue's hardwire kit for parking mode adds $29.99 (total $129.98), and a rideshare driver needs a 128 GB card to keep a full 8-hour shift, because a 64 GB card loops after 4.7 h. It does not rank the N4 above the Redtiger A3: the A3 costs $27.25 less and stays $21.25 cheaper with its kit, and the A3's hours per card could not be derived because no measured bitrate was found. The storage figure therefore supports the N4 row but does not decide the pick.

findings.label: Resolution with all three cameras recording (maker)
findings.value: 1440P + 1080P + 1080P at 30 fps (front, cabin, rear); the front alone records 2160P at 25 fps only in single-camera mode
findings.note: Vantrue's wording: 'recording front, inside cabin and road back simultaneously at 1440P+1080P+1080P at 30fps' and 'Single Front 4K (2160P@25fps)'. The same text names a Sony STARVIS sensor, a supercapacitor and 4 IR LEDs for the cabin.

findings.label: Measured bitrate per camera
findings.value: 15.3 Mb/s front (1440p), 8.3 Mb/s rear (1080p), 6.7 Mb/s cabin (1080p)
findings.note: DashCamTalk review published 2020-09-22. The same three figures are in forum member Sunny's review of 2020-02-14 (https://dashcamtalk.com/forum/threads/review-vantrue-n4-dashcam-3-channel-1440p-front-1080p-inside-cabin-1080p-rear.41834/). These are 2020 measurements; later firmware may differ.

findings.label: Derived: data written per hour with all three cameras recording
findings.note: 15.3 + 8.3 + 6.7 = 30.3 Mb/s; 30.3 ÷ 8 × 3,600 s = 13,635 MB = 13.6 GB per hour. Our arithmetic from DashCamTalk's bitrates; video only, decimal GB.

findings.label: Derived: hours of three-camera video before the loop overwrites
findings.value: 18.8 h on 256 GB; 9.4 h on 128 GB; 4.7 h on 64 GB; 2.3 h on 32 GB
findings.note: Card GB ÷ 13.6 GB/h (256 ÷ 13.635 = 18.8). Upper bound: assumes the whole card holds loop video, and locked event files and formatting reduce it. 256 GB is the maximum card in DashCamTalk's spec table; Sunny's review also quotes 'Supports up to 256GB microSD cards'.

findings.label: Derived: card needed to keep a full 8-hour driving shift
findings.value: 109 GB written in 8 h, so a 128 GB card (9.4 h); a 64 GB card keeps only the last 4.7 h
findings.note: 8 h × 13.6 GB/h = 109 GB. The 8-hour shift is our stated duty cycle, not a sourced figure.
